extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of federal education funding (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, campus administrators, legal counsel, and policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX complaint and complainant rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance on the definitions and procedural requirements for 'complainant' and 'complaint' under Title IX, including who may be a complainant, timing of participation, formats of complaints (oral/written), notice and recordkeeping obligations, and related training and reporting duties for recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'complainant' (participation/attempting to participate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Someone who is participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity (e.g., a prospective student, visiting student-athlete, guest speaker) can be a complainant even if not an enrolled student or employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether someone is participating or attempting to participate requires a fact-specific, case-by-case analysis. The participation requirement prevents a recipient from being legally obligated to initiate grievance procedures based on a complaint from a person having no relationship to the recipient. Examples include campus tours, sporting events, and lectures; a visitor may be a complainant depending on the reason for the visit and what the individual was doing at the time of the alleged discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of participation: assess at time of alleged discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The focus of the analysis is shifted from whether participation occurred at the time the complaint was filed to whether participation or attempted participation occurred at the time of the alleged sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring participation at the time of the alleged discrimination is aligned with Title IX's text and goal because it addresses conduct that would have interfered with the complainant's ability to participate in the recipient's education program or activity. This approach is consistent with relevant case law (e.g., Doe v. Brown Univ., Snyder-Hill v. Ohio State Univ.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: distinguish students/employees from other persons
rubrics_metrics.description: It is appropriate to distinguish between individuals who have a clear connection to the recipient (students and employees) and other individuals when determining who can be a complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department limits complainants to those participating or attempting to participate at the time of the alleged discrimination because Title IX does not impose a duty to address conduct that could not have excluded an individual from participating in or denied them benefits of the program. Visitors may be complainants only when a fact-based determination supports that they were participating or attempting to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'complaint' (oral or written; reasonable person standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'complaint' is an oral or written communication to the recipient that objectively can be understood as a request for the recipient to investigate and make a determination about alleged sex discrimination under Title IX and the implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complainant need not use any particular 'magic words' (e.g., 'initiate the recipient's grievance procedures'); the standard is whether a reasonable person could understand the communication as a request to investigate and make a determination. This is fact-specific but generally amounts to more than a student's general questions about grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of oral complaints (no writing/signature required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must accept complaints made orally as well as in writing; the Department declines to require a written complaint or signature to commence an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing oral complaints increases accessibility (including for students with disabilities and those with communication barriers) and reduces burdens that the 2020 signature/writing requirements imposed. Recipients remain responsible for following grievance procedures and ensuring fair process protections in §106.45 (and §106.46 where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping instead of mandatory written complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require some form of written documentation of the complaint to commence an investigation, instead relying on the recordkeeping obligations in §106.8(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(f) requires recipients to maintain records documenting informal resolution or grievance procedures and outcomes for each complaint, and records documenting actions taken when Title IX Coordinator receives notifications that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination. How to document oral reports is left to the recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent notice requirements (sufficient notice irrespective of format)
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure a fair resolution, a recipient must provide a respondent with sufficient notice of the allegations under §106.45(c), whether the complaint was made orally or in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While written complaints can help define investigation boundaries, they are neither necessary nor sufficient to ensure adequate notice. For postsecondary student complainants/respondents, §106.46(c) requires written notice. Recipients must provide notice upon initiation of grievance procedures per §106.45.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant autonomy and limits on compelled initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient should not initiate grievance procedures if a complainant does not want them initiated, except where the Title IX Coordinator determines the alleged conduct presents an imminent and serious threat to health or safety or prevents equal access per §106.44(f)(1)(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX Coordinators should confirm whether a complainant wants an investigation during initial conversations after explaining grievance procedures and supportive measures. The Coordinator may memorialize the outcome of that conversation in writing to avoid confusion. Nothing precludes a complainant from confirming or memorializing an oral complaint in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training obligations for Title IX Coordinator and designees
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.8(d) requires that the Title IX Coordinator and any designees be trained on a number of specific topics and receive any other training necessary to coordinate the recipient's compliance with Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to prescribe more detailed training on documenting oral reports beyond §106.8(d); recipients have discretion to choose the content and substance of additional training necessary for their context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation for non-confidential employees to report
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees who are not confidential employees must notify the Title IX Coordinator of any information they have about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, or provide the potential complainant with Title IX Coordinator contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A potential complainant who wants confidential support may seek out a confidential employee, if available. Information provided to a non-confidential employee that is reported to the Title IX Coordinator will only prompt a complaint without complainant permission if the Coordinator determines the imminent-threat factors in §106.44(f)(1)(v) are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator's role is not a confidential advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator is responsible for coordinating the recipient's compliance with Title IX, including providing information about grievance procedures and offering supportive measures, but is not a confidential advisor to the complainant or any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinators should carefully confirm allegations and whether the complainant intends to initiate grievance procedures. They may memorialize conversations to avoid confusion about next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'oral' rather than 'verbal'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department retains the word 'oral' rather than changing it to 'verbal' in the regulatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explains 'oral' is more precise for spoken communications; 'verbal' can ambiguously encompass written or spoken words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients cannot decline complaints for lack of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not deny a complaint solely because it was not submitted in writing; they must accept both oral and written complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revised definition aims to remove technical barriers created by the 2020 amendments (signed/written requirement) and promote reporting. Recipients still must follow grievance procedures and manage burdens; the Department finds any increased number of complaints justified by Title IX's nondiscrimination objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between complaints to recipients and complaints to OCR
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a distinction between a complaint made to a recipient (which may be oral or written under §106.2) and a complaint filed with OCR, which OCR requires to be in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complaint to OCR starts a federal administrative process with different consequences; the recipient-level complaint framework is intended to be accessible and responsive for time-sensitive, individualized matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities to offer supportive measures upon notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon actual knowledge of possible sexual harassment or notice of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, a recipient is required to offer supportive measures to a complainant, with or without a formal complaint, per §106.44(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation exists independently of complaint format; recipients should ensure supportive measures are available and offered promptly when appropriate.
